bull.b: Zscaler's subscription-based, per-user/device/workload pricing creates predictable, high-retention recurring revenue and sizable ARR. That model supports multi-year visibility, upsell/cross-sell to existing customers and steady cash conversion, underpinning durable top-line stability.

Consistent and growing operating and free cash flow provides durable financial flexibility to fund R&D, go-to-market expansion, strategic M&A, and higher near-term CapEx. Strong FCF supports balance sheet strengthening and reduces dependence on external financing over the medium term.

Rapid adoption of Zero Trust, growing data security ARR and AI-related bookings indicate a differentiated cloud-native platform with expanding use cases. Large enterprise wins, partner integrations and targeted acquisitions strengthen competitive moat and long-term cross-sell across customers.

bear.b: Despite improving gross and operating metrics, the company remains unprofitable on a GAAP basis with negative returns on equity. This indicates the transition to durable accounting profitability is incomplete and could constrain investor confidence and capital allocation flexibility.

Management's projection of mid-teens ARR/revenue growth for FY27 signals a structural slowing from prior high-teens to mid-20s growth. Slower organic net new ARR constrains long-term revenue expansion and reduces the pace at which the business can leverage fixed investment into higher operating profit.

Higher capital intensity and opportunistic pull-forward purchases driven by component cost/availability pressures reduce free-cash-flow margins and create variability in cash generation. Increased CapEx absorption can delay reinvestment payback and compress near-term capital returns.
